# consolidate worktree AFTER the 3/6 merge commit.

# CAVEAT: these scores do NOT include the uncommitted MS-YaHei font change to
# src/ggrender/render.go that lives in the card-atomic worktree. In particular
# lottery reads 0.98358 here, not the 0.98393 measured in that dirty worktree.
# (Re-measured on this branch: lottery = 0.98358, CAVEAT still holds.)
#
# --- round 4/6: feat/gg-render-recruit-headhunt @ 74c03a3, merged into consolidate/gg-mainline ---
# measured-at: 4bdbc64 (feat/gg-render-recruit-headhunt; integration of
#              feat/gg-render-headhunt into the ec440bf base)
# change:      headhunt only. Two commits, merged --no-ff as 4bdbc64:
#                5ad23b3  A-class asset wiring + SampleHeadhunt rarity data fix
#                          + geometry alignment      0.79983 -> 0.90357
#                df01ade  C-class portrait (amiya-half.webp)  0.90357 -> 0.96476
#              No gate logic touched, no similarityNormalized body touched, no
#              0.99 threshold touched, pixel_test.go / helpers.go / scene_card.go
#              untouched. render.go is the only source file changed, plus one
#              added binary asset (assets/headhunt/amiya-half.webp).
# verified:    independently by lead-8, NOT by the worker's own claim. A BEFORE
#              snapshot of all 16 scene lines was taken at ec440bf in a separate
#              worktree before any change, then diffed against the post-change
#              run. Result: exactly one line differs (headhunt). The other 15
#              scenes are byte-identical. The merge itself was also verified
#              (integration tree vs branch tip => diff_exit=0, i.e. the merge
#              changed no pixel).
# reproduce:   cd src && go test ./ggrender/ -run TestGGPixelParity -v
#
# provenance:  This file did NOT exist on feat/gg-render-card-atomic (ec440bf);
#              `git ls-tree -r --name-only ec440bf | grep pixel-parity-scores`
#              exits 1 with empty output. It was introduced by 0ea71c6
#              (fix/pixel-test-gofmt) and has copies on that branch plus
#              fix/gate-hardening (aa88012) and fix/card-text-color (5331064),
#              each reflecting that branch's own change point. This copy is
#              created on feat/gg-render-recruit-headhunt.
#              Evidence for the "not on ec440bf" claim:
#                git merge-base --is-ancestor 0ea71c6 ec440bf   => exit 1
#                git branch --contains 0ea71c6 => fix/card-text-color,
#                                                fix/gate-hardening,
#                                                fix/pixel-test-gofmt
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CAVEAT
#
# 1. This baseline does NOT include the uncommitted MS-YaHei font change to
#    src/ggrender/render.go that lives in the card-atomic worktree. In
#    particular lottery reads 0.98358 here, not the 0.98393 measured in that
#    dirty worktree.
#
# 2. Three scenes measure a DEGENERATE FIXTURE, not a realistic render. Passing
#    0.99 on them says the renderer faithfully reproduces a degraded fixture —
#    it does NOT say the scene is correct under real data:
#      · headhunt — the 10 ops share ONE ThumbURL, so the baseline draws 10
#        identical portraits. Rendering 10 DIFFERENT operators would score
#        WORSE. headhunt at 0.99 would not mean headhunt is right.
#      · recruit  — resource-manifest.json declares exactly ONE resource whose
#        target mentions Recruit (cache/amiya-avatar.webp), so the baseline
#        draws the same Amiya portrait in all 14 slots. Same caveat.
#      · box     — 11 identical Amiya cards; the template's
#        onerror="this.src='assets/common/amiya.png'" fallback is what fired.
#    NOTE: for headhunt and recruit this is FIXTURE DEGENERATION, not
#    onerror degradation. requestStats shows failedRequests/fallbackCount/
#    missingResources all zero for all 16 scenes — that field returns the same
#    answer for every input (including the known-degraded box), so it carries
#    zero information and must NOT be used to classify a scene.
#
# 3. Two measured NET-NEGATIVE results, recorded so nobody repeats them:
#      · Restoring the baseline's 2 tag groups (recruit class-B structure
#        repair): 0.61351 -> 0.54379 (-0.06972). A pure-refactor CONTROL
#        reproduced 0.61351 exactly, so the drop is attributable to the
#        structure change, not refactor noise. Root cause: ScaleToManifest
#        hard-stretches the natural canvas to 1350x534, so any change that
#        alters canvas height changes the global scale and misaligns
#        everything. Fixing class B requires fixing the scaling first (D2).
#      · Deleting content we draw that the baseline does not have is ALSO
#        net-negative before the background is fixed: 0.61351 -> 0.57894
#        (-0.03457). The extra pixels are currently NOT deep-background, and
#        deep-background is our single most expensive error (27.61% of diff
#        mass). Deleting them is removing a fig leaf, not a correction.
#    Generalised: a scalar similarity gate rewards drawing MORE over drawing
#    MORE-ACCURATELY whenever un-drawn area is penalised differently. For any
#    low-scoring scene, ask first "is something over-drawn masking a bigger
#    error?" — not "what is missing?"
#
# 4. headhunt 0.96476 vs the 0.99 gate: PART of the gap is NOT a rendering
#    defect but an ENCODING PATH difference. The frozen baseline is a Chromium
#    JPEG screenshot (lossy, 4:2:0 chroma subsampling, measured 16/16); our
#    output is a lossless re-encode from the original webp. The compression
#    damage on the baseline side cannot be removed without reproducing that
#    damage. Injecting matching quantisation noise would be a BASELINE-DERIVED
#    ASSET, which this project forbids — the red line concerns the asset's
#    PROVENANCE, not the file extension, and re-encoding does not change the
#    provenance. Therefore 0.96476 must NOT be read as "adjust the geometry and
#    it will reach 0.99". The geometry is already aligned; the one genuinely
#    improvable region is the right strip (RMS 16.998, a 25px seam
#    extrapolation), not a re-encode.
#
# 5. Boundary observed when fixing SampleHeadhunt's data:
#      INPUT must match the baseline's input. GEOMETRY/COORDINATES must be
#      computed by the renderer, never back-derived from the baseline image.
#    What was changed is the DATA VALUE (Rarity), justified by two
#    baseline-independent facts: the old Rarity: 3+i%4 produced two ops with
#    Rarity=6, and back_6.png / Rarity_6.png DO NOT EXIST under
#    assets/headhunt/ (i.e. the renderer was reading a non-existent asset and
#    drawing no star bar at all — this needs no score argument); and
#    Rarity_5.png was proven to hold 6 stars by connected-component counting
#    while Rarity_0..4 hold 1..5. NOT ONE coordinate was copied off the
#    baseline image. If you ever see someone editing fixture COORDINATES to
#    raise the score, that is the line being crossed.
#    Same boundary applied to assets/headhunt/amiya-half.webp: the CHOICE of
#    that image is input-side and is proven by a format-level impossibility
#    (all 16 baseline images are JPEG mode=RGB with no alpha channel, while
#    this file is WebP RGBA with alpha extrema (0,255) — it cannot be a crop
#    of any of them). Its placement and scale were derived from the asset's
#    own 180x360 = 1:2 ratio and the pixel-measured 95x190 = 1:2 frame, not
#    from measuring the baseline jpg.
#
# 6. Known gate limitations (quoted from docs/audit/verifier-review-20260929.md,
#    2026-09-29 verifier review; sign-off "conditional pass, 4 must-fix + 1
#    ruled unimplementable and recorded as a known limitation"):
#      · Defect #6, self-validating trust anchor [UNFIXED]: pixel_test.go's
#        hash gate only checks "baseline file sha256 == the sha256 in the same
#        manifest record", and both can be changed together. Replacing the
#        baseline with a self-made image AND updating the manifest sha256 still
#        passes every check. The only defence today is git tracking plus human
#        review — that is not a cryptographic anchor.
#      · Defect #7, baseline as backdrop plus small perturbation [UNHANDLED]:
#        sim >= 0.99 permits sum <= 0.01*w*h*4*255 and a single pixel can
#        contribute 765, so roughly 1.33% of the canvas can be completely
#        wrong and still pass. Measured: gatePassed(0.9995, non-empty bbox)
#        returns true.
#    When you read ANY 0.99xx score in this file, you must know these two.
#
# 7. Gate limitation in the OPPOSITE direction — over-strict, not over-lenient:
#    single-pixel differences are killed. Per ruling, NOT fixed. A legitimate
#    near-perfect render (measured single-pixel difference sim=0.99992) is
#    judged a gate failure, because the zero-area bbox guard uses closed-interval
#    semantics and a single-pixel difference yields [x,y,x,y], which is
#    numerically indistinguishable from the zero-difference [0,0,0,0]. Not
#    fixing it is a RULING, not an oversight: the fix would require relaxing the
#    zero-span test from <= 0 to < 0, which is relaxing the gate. (The sentinel
#    has since been changed to [-1,-1,-1,-1] so the two cases are separable in
#    value, yet BOTH are still judged failures.)
#    Together with items 6 and 7: the gate may let 1.33% of the canvas be wrong,
#    and may also reject sim=0.99992. THE BIAS IS BIDIRECTIONAL. Do not read
#    this harness as merely lenient.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
